Milica was the name of several saints in Eastern Orthodox Church. The name Milica carries the meaning “Gracious Gift of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Milica usually hope their child will grow to embody gracious gift of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: מיליצה
in_hebrew.meaning: מיליצה היא שם שפירושו עמי או עם שלי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מיליצה הוא שם שמקורו בשפה הסלאבית, אך יש לו קשרים רבים עם השפה העברית והתרבות היהודית. המילה 'מיליצה' נגזרת מהמילה הסלאבית 'מיל', שפירושها 'עמי' או 'עם שלי'. שם זה נמצא בשימוש נרחב בקרב הנוצרים והוא מקושר לקונספט של קהילה ושייכות.

in_greek.name: Μίλιτσα
in_greek.meaning: Μίλιτσα σημαίνει του λαού μου ή ο λαός μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μίλιτσα έχει σλαβική προέλευση, αλλά έχει συσχετισμούς με την ελληνική και τη χριστιανική παράδοση. Η λέξη 'Μίλιτσα' προέρχεται από τη σλαβική λέξη 'μίλ', που σημαίνει 'του λαού μου' ή 'ο λαός μου'. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν κοινό ανάμεσα στους Χριστιανούς και συνδέεται με την έννοια της κοινότητας και της ταυτότητας.

historical_references.reference: Milica, the daughter of Vukasin Mrnjavčević, was a prominent figure in the Serbian medieval history. She was born in the early 14th century and was known for her exceptional beauty and intelligence. Milica played a significant role during the Serbian resistance against the Ottoman Turks. In 1331, she married Stephen Uroš IV Dušan, who later became the King of Serbia. Milica's influence on her husband helped him to achieve important victories against the Byzantines and the Bulgarians, expanding the Serbian territory significantly.

historical_references.reference: Another Milica, who lived in the 15th century, was a religious figure and the founder of the Monastery of the Holy Savior in Šumadija, Serbia. Born into a noble family, she dedicated her life to Christianity and became a nun. Milica is revered as a saint in the Serbian Orthodox Church, and her intercession is believed to protect women in childbirth and those seeking healing from illness.
